project_scope.note: Two canonical local anchors are live: Opuntia engelmannii var. lindheimeri and O. macrorhiza. Source-row O. senilis remaps to accepted O. orbiculata but remains HOLD because the current Central Texas delimitation/county package is not clean enough. O. phaeacantha also remains HOLD: current Kew accepts the species, but the old Kerr WMA name O. phaeacantha var. major now maps to O. gilvescens and cannot be counted as present-day O. phaeacantha evidence.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Find an areole before anything else. It is the specialized structure that produces spines, hairs, branches and flowers.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Succulent stems vary widely; mature leaves are often reduced or absent.
family_diagnostics.flower: Usually many perianth segments and many stamens; ovary inferior.
family_diagnostics.opuntia: Pads are flattened stem segments (cladodes), not leaves; Opuntioideae adds barbed glochids at areoles.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Succulence is not enough—true cactus areoles are the key.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: The whole cactus lesson can start with one question: can you find an areole?

steps.title: 1 · Learn the local Opuntia form
steps.look_for: Flattened stem segments carrying repeated areoles.
steps.why_it_matters: The pad is a stem; the areoles are the defining cactus structures.

steps.title: 2 · Put the flower on an areole
steps.image_credit: Public Domain · Clarence A. Rechenthin / USDA-NRCS
steps.look_for: A large flower arising from an areole near the pad margin.
steps.why_it_matters: Shows that areoles produce flowers as well as spines and shoots.

steps.title: 3 · Zoom into areole + glochids
steps.look_for: A small cushion-like areole bearing fine barbed glochids and/or larger spines.
steps.why_it_matters: Glochids are an Opuntioideae specialization layered onto the family-wide areole.

steps.title: 4 · Follow flower to fruit
steps.look_for: The ovary is below the perianth; mature fruit is fleshy and many-seeded.
steps.why_it_matters: Reproductive anatomy confirms the family beyond the succulent habit.

steps.title: 5 · Compare the low grassland pricklypear
steps.look_for: A low, spreading plant with smaller pads, orange-brown glochids, and often a few strongly bent or deflexed permanent spines.
steps.why_it_matters: This gives the crew a real local Opuntia comparison against the larger Texas-pricklypear anchor.

comparisons.title: Cactaceae vs Euphorbiaceae
comparisons.rule: Succulent Euphorbia can mimic a cactus but lacks true areoles.

comparisons.title: Cactaceae vs Yucca/Agave
comparisons.rule: Yucca and Agave have true fibrous leaves in rosettes; cacti center their growth on areoles and highly modified/reduced leaves.

visual_lesson.caveat: Two taxonomy guardrails: O. lindheimeri is the same learner concept as accepted O. engelmannii var. lindheimeri; source-row O. senilis maps to O. orbiculata but stays HOLD. Do not count historical O. phaeacantha var. major records toward current O. phaeacantha because current Kew treats var. major under O. gilvescens.
